I couldn't find how to put a list of items inside a request body in the FastAPI docs provided. They cover single Pydantic models as request bodies, but not models containing lists.

Here's what the docs do cover. To declare a **request** body, you use Pydantic models with all their power and benefits.[1] For example:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel


class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None
    price: float
    tax: float | None = None


app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/items/")
async def create_item(item: Item):
    return item
```

If the parameter is declared to be of the type of a **Pydantic model**, it will be interpreted as a request **body**.[5] Also, to send data, you should use one of: `POST` (the most common), `PUT`, `DELETE` or `PATCH`.[1]

Source: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/body/

For an order containing a list of items, look in the FastAPI tutorial for the section on nested models or list fields in request bodies.
